subtitle: Malik Ambar’s Measure of the Land

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Malik Ambar overlooking terraced fields and village surveyors
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands on a rocky outcrop, hand resting on a rolled revenue register, watching his officers pace out fields and examine standing crops across a sunlit Deccan valley.

dialogue.text: In Malik Ambar’s Deccan, armies rode on silver from the soil, and every grain counted—yet his new measures could protect villages or press them hard. How did one man reshape the land’s account?

i18n.hi: मलिक अम्बर के दक्खन में, खेतों की चाँदी पर फ़ौजें चलतीं, हर दाना अहम था—उसकी नई नाप गाँव बचाती भी, दबाती भी। एक आदमी ने ज़मीन का हिसाब कैसे बदल दिया?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Malik Ambar in council chamber
panels.action: Inside a stone hall in Ahmadnagar, Malik Ambar sits at a low desk strewn with palm-leaf records and maps, listening as village officials and soldiers argue over revenue demands.

dialogue.text: Around 1610, the Ahmadnagar state strained for coin. Old jagirdars squeezed villages; cavalry went unpaid; fields lay uncertain under shifting claims.

i18n.hi: लगभग १६१० में अहमदनगर में सिक्के की किल्लत थी। पुराने जागीरदार गाँव निचोड़ रहे थे; घुड़सवारों को तनख़्वाह नहीं; खेत दावों की उठापटक में अधर में थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Malik Ambar turning from soldiers to village headmen
panels.action: Malik Ambar raises a hand to silence armored horsemen, turning instead to humble village headmen seated on mats, their faces lined with worry.

dialogue.text: Malik Ambar had risen from enslaved youth in the Deccan to regent of Ahmadnagar. Now he sought control of land revenue to steady both fort and field.

i18n.hi: दक्खन में ग़ुलाम बालक से उठकर मलिक अम्बर अहमदनगर का वज़ीर बना। अब वह क़िले और खेत दोनों सँभालने को लगान पर क़ाबू चाहता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Deccan village with officers arriving
panels.action: Deccan Revenue Officers ride into a dusty village, dismounting with measuring ropes and writing boards as farmers pause from their work to watch.

dialogue.text: Instead of leaving extraction to jagirdars alone, Ambar’s officials went to the villages. They walked the soil, saw the crops, and sought direct settlements.

i18n.hi: जागीरदारों पर छोड़ने के बजाय, अम्बर के अफ़सर सीधे गाँव पहुँचे। मिट्टी पर चले, फ़सल देखी, और सीधे मोल-तोल किया।

panels.shot: overhead view of officers stretching ropes across a field
panels.action: Revenue officers stretch knotted ropes across a green field while a farmer stands nearby, pointing to boundary stones and irrigation channels.

dialogue.text: They practiced kankut—measuring the land and estimating the harvest. Ropes marked length; the officers’ eyes, and local knowledge, judged the standing crop.

i18n.hi: वे ‘कनकूत’ करते थे—ज़मीन नापते, पैदावार आँकते। रस्सियाँ लंबाई बाँधतीं; अफ़सरों की आँखें और देसी समझ खड़ी फसल को तौलतीं।

panels.shot: close-up of officer’s hand examining crop stalks
panels.action: An officer crouches, fingers lightly weighing handfuls of grain stalks, while another notes figures on a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Height of stalks, thickness of ears, spread of irrigation—all entered the calculation. The estimate became the basis of the state’s claim.

i18n.hi: तनों की ऊँचाई, बालियों की मोटाई, पानी की पहुँच—सब हिसाब में आता। यही अंदाज़ा राज्य की माँग की नींव बनता।

panels.shot: medium shot of officer and farmer seated under tree negotiating
panels.action: Under a broad tree, a revenue officer and a farmer sit facing each other; the officer points to a rough map and figures while the farmer counts on his fingers, hesitant.

dialogue.text: With kankut, Ambar’s men fixed cash demands on what the land could yield. Villagers bargained, pointing to risks of rain, pests, and cattle disease.

i18n.hi: कनकूत से अम्बर के लोग ज़मीन की शक्ल पर नक़द लगान बाँधते। गाँव वाले बरसात, कीड़े-मकोड़े, मवेशी रोग का डर दिखा कर भिड़ते।

panels.shot: close-up on officer’s serious face listening to farmer
panels.action: The officer leans forward, brows furrowed, listening as the farmer speaks urgently, gesturing back toward a clouded horizon.

dialogue.speaker: Farmer
dialogue.text: Sir, if the monsoon fails, how will we pay such a sum?

i18n.hi: हुज़ूर, अगर बरसात ही धोखा दे गई तो इतना पैसा कहाँ से देंगे?

panels.shot: wide shot of Ambar’s officers in a Balaghat landscape
panels.action: Revenue officers traverse undulating Balaghat terrain—some crossing streams, others skirting forest edges—with scribes and local guides in tow.

dialogue.text: In the Balaghat and western Deccan, fields, forest, and pasture mixed. Andre Wink notes that Ambar’s system had to reckon with such varied ecologies.

i18n.hi: बलाघाट और पश्चिमी दक्खन में खेत, जंगल, चरागाह घुले-मिले थे। आंद्रे विंक लिखते हैं, अम्बर की नाप-तौल को इन बदले-रूप इलाकों का भी हिसाब रखना पड़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot inside village meeting with intermediaries
panels.action: Inside a village house, an officer sits with local intermediaries—patils, deshmukhs, and moneylenders—while a scribe records their agreements.

dialogue.text: As Sumit Guha shows, these settlements relied on local power-brokers. Ambar’s officers could not sweep them aside; they bargained and shared authority.

i18n.hi: जैसा सुमित गुवा बताते हैं, ये सौदे देसी असरदारों पर टिके थे। अम्बर के अफ़सर उन्हें हटा नहीं सकते थे; उन्हें भी साथ लेकर, बाँटकर चलना पड़ता था।

panels.shot: close-up of palm-leaf register being filled
panels.action: A scribe carefully inscribes lines of script onto a palm leaf, listing fields, crop types, and cash dues, while a small heap of silver coins lies nearby.

dialogue.text: Names of cultivators, size of plots, expected yield, agreed cash—everything entered the registers. The state’s memory of the land grew sharper.

i18n.hi: किसानों के नाम, टुकड़ों का आकार, अनुमानित फ़सल, तय नक़द—सब रजिस्टरों में दर्ज हुआ। राज्य की ज़मीन की याद और पैनी हो गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Malik Ambar inspecting compiled records
panels.action: Back in Ahmadnagar, Malik Ambar stands over a table stacked with bound registers as officers present summaries; behind him, armored cavalry wait in the courtyard.

dialogue.text: Thomas Elphinstone later admired these detailed accounts. He thought Ambar had pioneered a kind of ryotwari—direct settlement with cultivators.

i18n.hi: थॉमस एल्फ़िन्स्टन ने बाद में इन बारीक हिसाबों की दाद दी। उसे लगा, अम्बर ने एक तरह की रैयतवारी—सीधी किसान से बात—की नींव रखी।

panels.shot: close-up on Ambar’s contemplative face between a register and a spear rack
panels.action: Malik Ambar’s face is caught between lamplight on a register and the shadowed outline of spears and shields on the wall.

dialogue.text: Modern historians caution: this was no simple invention. It was a web of bargains, made to feed an army as much as to ease a ploughman’s load.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार टोकते हैं: यह कोई एक सीधी चाल नहीं थी। यह सौदों का जाल था—फ़ौज को खिलाने जितना, हल चलाने वाले का बोझ घटाने को भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of cavalry drilling outside city walls
panels.action: Deccan cavalry train in a dusty field outside the city walls while pay-chests are opened and coins counted by officials nearby.

dialogue.text: With fuller coffers, Ambar could pay his troops and resist Mughal pressure. Land records turned into horses, muskets, and fortified hill posts.

i18n.hi: खज़ाना भरकर अम्बर अपनी फ़ौज को तनख़्वाह दे सका और मुग़ल दबाव झेल सका। ज़मीन के काग़ज़ घोड़े, बंदूकें और किलेबंद पहाड़ी चौकियाँ बन गए।

panels.shot: medium shot in a village grain store during poor harvest
panels.action: In a dim grain store, farmers stand uneasily beside half-empty bins as an officer compares the meagre piles with figures on his register.

dialogue.text: But when harvests failed, fixed cash demands bit hard. Detailed records did not always mean mercy; they could also enforce exact dues.

i18n.hi: पर जब फ़सलें मारी गईं, तय नक़द लगान ने काट लिया। बारीक रजिस्टर करुणा की गारंटी नहीं थे; वे सही-सही वसूली भी करवा सकते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of farmer’s weary face as he offers a small coin
panels.action: A farmer, tired and anxious, extends a lone silver coin with both hands toward the officer, children watching from behind a doorway.

dialogue.speaker: Farmer
dialogue.text: We have given the grain. Now only this remains.

i18n.hi: अनाज तो दे दिया। अब बस इतना ही बचा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of officer hesitating, glancing between farmer and register
panels.action: The officer pauses, eyes shifting from the farmer’s outstretched hands to the rigid lines of calculation on the palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Here lay the tension in Ambar’s system: the officer stood between numbers that sustained the state and faces that bore the weight.

i18n.hi: यही खिंचाव अम्बर की नाप में था: अफ़सर उन अंकों के बीच खड़ा था जो राज्य को सँभालते, और उन चेहरों के बीच जो भार उठाते।

panels.shot: wide shot of village at dusk with both prosperity and strain visible
panels.action: At dusk, a Deccan village shows new wells and bunded fields on one side, while on the other a family sells a bullock to a moneylender outside his house.

dialogue.text: Some villages gained stability—wells dug, bunds raised, disputes recorded. Others slid deeper into debt as cash demands met uncertain skies.

i18n.hi: कुछ गाँवों को राहत मिली—कुएँ खोदे गए, बांध उठे, झगड़े दर्ज हुए। कुछ और करज़ में धँस गए, जब नक़द की माँग बदले आसमानों से टकराई।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Ambar’s records to a later British officer referencing them
panels.action: The image transitions from Malik Ambar’s palm-leaf registers on a wooden table to a later British officer in uniform reading an 1819 report that cites those Deccan precedents.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, British officials praised Ambar as father of their ryotwari. Yet his legacy is more tangled: he taught that power rests on knowing the land—and that justice must watch every measure.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद अंग्रेज़ अफ़सरों ने अम्बर को अपनी रैयतवारी का जनक कहा। पर उसकी विरासत उलझी हुई है: उसने दिखाया ताक़त ज़मीन को जानने पर टिकी है—और इंसाफ़ को हर नाप पर नज़र रखनी पड़ती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Malik Ambar’s Measure of the Land
subtitle_i18n.hi: मलिक अम्बर की ज़मीन की नाप
